title: task list's manifest fields advertise a 13-name subset of the record's top-level keys
description: Surfaced by QCLI-312 while building --fields under DEC-161: the accept-set for --fields is the fields quest manifest --json advertises for the command (ruling A), and for task list that advertised set is 13 names while task list --json items carry more top-level keys (measured: a migrated record 24 keys, a native one 19). So a field a record genuinely carries (e.g. description, plan, acceptanceCriteria, implementationNotes) is not advertised and --fields rejects it. The pre-existing contract test asserts only declared subset-of payload, never payload subset-of declared, so nothing catches the understatement. Not DEC-161 work and not started there.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Quest manifest --json advertises for task list every top-level key a task list item carries (payload is a subset of declared), asserted in that direction by a test, not only declared-subset-of-payload
The help or the manifest states unambiguously what a command fields array means when the payload varies by record (a curated subset vs a complete key set), so a consumer can tell which it is reading
